speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Please tell me, exactly how did your right groin pain start, and have you noticed any abnormal positioning of your leg since that rear-end collision?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a distinct "pop" or "snap" sound at the moment of injury, and was your right knee initially hyperextended? Also, what is your current ability to bear weight on that leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation. The clinical picture of a rear-end collision, immediate severe groin pain, and the classic "shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated" leg position is pathognomonic for this injury. I am requesting a Pelvis_XRay and Hip_XRay to confirm the diagnosis and rule out associated fractures.
